Basic Combat Rules

In addition to the written class rules for each class, all classes share a few things: Every time a character levels up, they gain +1 to any two stats they choose (or +2 to one stat). On levels 3, 6, 9 and 12, they gain a Feat Level 12 is the max level

Core Character and Combat Rules Ability Scores Every character possesses six ability scores representing their natural capabilities. ●Strength (STR): Physical power, lifting, grappling, and brute force. ●Dexterity (DEX): Reflexes, precision, coordination, and agility. ●Constitution (CON): Endurance, toughness, resistance to poison, disease, and physical punishment. ●Intelligence (INT): Reasoning, technical knowledge, investigation, and scientific understanding. ●Wisdom (WIS): Awareness, intuition, judgment, and perception. ●Charisma (CHA): Persuasion, intimidation, deception, and force of personality.

Ability scores determine modifiers using the following formula: Ability Modifier = floor((Ability Score − 10) / 2) Ability Score Modifier 1 −5 2–3 −4 4–5 −3 6–7 −2 8–9 −1 10–11 +0 12–13 +1 14–15 +2 16–17 +3 18–19 +4 20–21 +5 22–23 +6 24–25 +7

Starting Ability Scores At character creation, players may choose either the Standard Array or Point Buy method. Both methods provide equivalent starting ability scores. Standard Array: Assign the following six scores to the six abilities in any order: 15, 14, 13, 12, 10, 8 Point Buy: Players receive 27 points to distribute among their six ability scores. Every ability begins at 8, and no ability may exceed 15 during character creation. Ability Score Point Cost 8 0 9 1
10 2 11 3 12 4 13 5 14 7 15 9 Both methods use the same point budget, although Point Buy allows players to distribute their scores differently.

Attack Rolls When a character attempts to strike, shoot, stab, pulverize, or otherwise injure a creature, they make an attack roll. Attack Roll = d20 + Attack Ability Modifier + Proficiency Bonus (if proficient) The attack succeeds if its total equals or exceeds the target's Armor Class (AC). An attack roll represents more than whether a weapon physically makes contact. A failed attack might miss entirely, glance off armor, be dodged, or strike without causing meaningful injury. Attack Ability Modifiers ●Melee weapons: Strength ●Ranged weapons: Dexterity ●Unarmed attacks: Strength ●Thrown weapons: Strength, unless the weapon specifies otherwise ●Finesse weapons: Strength or Dexterity, chosen by the attacker

Individual weapons, mutations, and class abilities may specify alternative ability modifiers. Weapon Proficiency A character adds their Proficiency Bonus to attacks made with weapons they are proficient in. Attacks with unfamiliar weapons can still be attempted, but do not receive the Proficiency Bonus. Natural 20s and Natural 1s A natural 20 on an attack roll always hits and is a Critical Hit, regardless of the target's AC. A natural 1 on an attack roll always misses, regardless of modifiers. Natural 20s and natural 1s do not automatically succeed or fail on ordinary ability checks. The GM may introduce exceptional narrative consequences where appropriate. Advantage and Disadvantage

When a character has advantage, they roll two d20s and use the higher result. When they have disadvantage, they roll two d20s and use the lower result. Multiple sources of advantage do not stack. Multiple sources of disadvantage do not stack. If both advantage and disadvantage apply, they cancel, regardless of how many sources of each are present. Damage and Critical Hits When an attack hits, the attacker rolls the weapon's damage dice and adds the appropriate ability modifier. Damage = Weapon Damage Dice + Attack Ability Modifier + Other Applicable Bonuses Damage cannot be reduced below zero. Damage reduces the target's current HP. Weapon damage dice are determined by the weapon being used. Particularly powerful weapons,

explosives, mutations, and class abilities may use additional dice or special damage rules. Critical Hits When an attack scores a Critical Hit, roll twice the normal number of damage dice. For example, a weapon that normally deals 2d6 + 3 damage instead deals 4d6 + 3 on a Critical Hit. Flat modifiers are not doubled unless an ability explicitly states otherwise. Damage Types Damage may be described as ballistic, slashing, piercing, bludgeoning, fire, cold, electrical, chemical, radiation, psychic, energy, blast, or another appropriate type at DM discretion. Damage types have no special mechanical effect by default. However, creatures, armor, equipment, mutations, and abilities may provide resistance, vulnerability, or immunity to particular types.

●Resistance: Halve incoming damage of the specified type, rounding down. ●Vulnerability: Double incoming damage of the specified type. ●Immunity: Take no damage of the specified type. Radiation Damage Whenever a creature takes radiation damage from a weapon, if the unmodified to-hit (or placement, for area attacks) check was 15 or higher and the attack hit, the target suffers some extra radioactive effects. If the unmodified to-hit(or placement, for area attacks) check was 5 or lower, the attacker makes the check, as their weapon has betrayed them. Radioactive side effects Side effects are one of the 12 following options. Roll a D12 to determine which one. 1 Glowstick

The target glows bright green for 3 turns. It cannot benefit from being invisible or hidden in darkness. 2 Nuclear Hiccups The target emits radioactive hiccups. Disadvantage on Stealth checks for 3 turns. 3 Magnetic Personality Loose metal objects cling to the target. Movement speed is reduced by 10 ft for 2 turns. 4 Bone Rattle The target's skeleton vibrates violently. Disadvantage on its next attack roll. 5 Radioactive Flatulence A 10-ft cloud forms around the target. Creatures inside must make a CON save or

become Poisoned until the end of their next turn. 6 Third Eye The target temporarily grows an extra eye. Advantage on Perception checks for 3 turns. 7 Meat Magnet The target becomes unnaturally attractive to nearby hostile creatures. Enemies have advantage on their next attack against it. 8 Unscheduled Growth One limb doubles in size for 3 turns. The target gains +2 melee damage but disadvantage on Dexterity checks. 9 Geiger Counter

The target emits loud clicking sounds for 3 turns, revealing its approximate location. 10 Sudden Evolution The target gains +10 ft movement speed for 2 turns. Its next movement must be in a straight line. 11 Atomic Sneeze The target violently sneezes radioactive mucus. Every creature within 5 ft takes 1d4 radiation damage, including allies. 12 Critical Mass The target immediately suffers another 1d6 radiation damage. Roll again on this table, ignoring another result of Critical Mass. Damage and Healing

A creature's current HP cannot exceed its maximum HP. When a creature receives healing, it regains the specified amount of HP, up to its maximum. Healing has no effect on a dead creature unless the effect explicitly allows revival. Death and Mutation Revival There is no downed or dying state in 501 Rads. When a character's HP reaches 0, they immediately die. They do not fall unconscious, make death saving throws, or receive an opportunity to stabilize. Death immediately initiates the Mutation Revival process, as described in the mutation rules. This entails a 30 minute wait and a new negative mutation, reviving with 1 hp. Characters cannot be restored through ordinary healing once they have died. Extraordinary

abilities may interact with death or revival only when explicitly permitted by their descriptions. A character who returns through Mutation Revival suffers whatever consequences that process entails. There is no distinction between ordinary lethal damage and massive damage. Any attack or effect that reduces a character to 0 HP is lethal. Total Bodily Destruction: Mutation Revival occurs regardless of the extent of bodily damage. A character may regenerate from dismemberment, incineration, vaporization, or even complete atomic disintegration. After 30 minutes, the character is fully reconstituted with 1 HP and gains one negative mutation, following the normal Mutation Revival rules.

No physical remains are required. The mechanism behind this phenomenon is unknown, poorly understood, and frankly none of your business. The Game Master determines where the character reconstitutes if their original location is inaccessible or otherwise unsuitable. Skills and Proficiency Skills represent specific areas of training, experience, and practical competence. When a character attempts a task with an uncertain outcome, the GM may request an ability check. Ability Check = d20 + Relevant Ability Modifier + Proficiency Bonus (if proficient)

The GM determines which ability and skill are most appropriate to the task. Players may suggest alternative approaches, but the GM makes the final determination. The GM should not require a roll for tasks that are trivial, impossible, or have no meaningful consequences for failure. The GM should not allow rolls for actions that will never be possible. Starting Skill Proficiencies At level 1, every character chooses four skills in which they are proficient. Two of these must use one of the character's primary class ability scores as their usual modifier. The other two may be chosen freely. A proficient character adds their Proficiency Bonus to checks involving that skill. Characters cannot select the same proficiency twice to receive a double bonus.

Saving Throw Proficiencies Each class is proficient in saving throws using its two primary ability scores. Class Saving Throw Proficiencies Gunslinger Dexterity, Charisma Psycho Strength, Charisma Hacker Dexterity, Intelligence Medic Constitution, Intelligence Soldier Strength, Wisdom Prophet Dexterity, Wisdom When making a saving throw in which they are proficient, characters add their Proficiency Bonus to the relevant ability modifier. Saving Throw = d20 + Ability Modifier + Proficiency Bonus (if proficient)

Expertise Expertise represents extraordinary specialization in a skill. A character with Expertise adds twice their Proficiency Bonus, rather than the normal amount, when making checks using that skill. Expertise is not granted automatically. It must be acquired through a feat, class ability, mutation, or other explicitly defined feature. Expertise never stacks with itself. Proficiency and Expertise Through Feats When a character selects a Feat that grants proficiency in a skill or weapon category, the following rules apply: ●Not Proficient: The character gains proficiency in the specified skill or weapon category.

●Already Proficient: The character instead gains Expertise in the specified skill or weapon category. ●Already an Expert: The Feat provides no additional proficiency benefit. Expertise doubles the character's Proficiency Bonus for the relevant skill checks or weapon attack rolls. Expertise does not stack with itself. A character may select each Feat only once. Consequently, characters cannot acquire Expertise by selecting the same training Feat twice. Feats that grant a choice of proficiencies require the character to select which proficiency receives the benefit when the Feat is acquired. Character Statistics Every class in 501 Rads has its own base Hit Points (HP), Hit Die, Armor Class (AC), and Movement Speed. These statistics reflect the

natural strengths and weaknesses of each class. Characters improve their survivability through leveling, ability scores, equipment, and class abilities. Class Statistics Class Primary Stats Hit Die Level 1 HP Fixed HP / Level Base AC Unarmored AC Cap Movement Gunslinger DEX / CHA d8 8 + CON mod 5 + CON mod 7 18 35 ft Psycho STR / CHA d12 12 + CON mod 7 + CON mod 9 20 40 ft Hacker DEX / INT d6 6 + CON mod 4 + CON mod 6 16 30 ft Medic CON / INT d10 10 + CON mod 6 + CON mod 7 18 30 ft Soldier STR / WIS d12 12 + CON mod 7 + CON mod 8 20 35 ft Prophet DEX / WIS d8 8 + CON mod 5 + CON mod 7 16 25 ft Hit Points and Leveling At level 1, characters receive the maximum value of their class's Hit Die plus their Constitution modifier. At every subsequent level, they may either roll their class's Hit Die or take the

fixed HP increase listed above, adding their Constitution modifier in either case. Characters always gain at least 1 maximum HP per level. If a character's Constitution modifier increases or decreases, their maximum HP is adjusted retroactively by 1 HP per character level for each point of modifier change. During a short rest, characters may spend available Hit Dice to recover HP. Characters have a number of Hit Dice equal to their character level, and each spent die restores the amount rolled plus their Constitution modifier, to a minimum of 1 HP. Long rests restore all HP and spent Hit Dice. Armor Class Armor Class determines how difficult a character is to hit. Unlike systems where armor establishes a fixed AC, armor in 501 Rads provides a bonus to the character's natural defenses.

AC = min(Base Class AC + Primary Physical Stat Modifier, Unarmored AC Cap) + Armor Bonus Each class uses its designated primary physical ability score to calculate AC: Strength for Psychos and Soldiers, Constitution for Medics, and Dexterity for Gunslingers, Hackers, and Prophets. The unarmored AC cap limits the combined contribution of base class AC and the primary physical modifier. Armor bonuses are applied afterward and may raise a character's AC above that cap. Armor Category AC Bonus Ordinary clothing +0 Light armor +1 Medium armor +2 Heavy armor +3

Powered armor +4 Armor bonuses do not stack unless an item or ability explicitly states otherwise. The highest possible AC from these standard rules is 24, achieved by a Psycho or Soldier at their unarmored cap while wearing powered armor. Exceptional equipment, mutations, or abilities may modify AC further if explicitly permitted. Movement Movement Speed represents the distance a character can move during their turn without sacrificing their normal action. Characters may move up to their listed speed and still perform an action. A character may spend their action to Dash, moving an additional distance equal to their Movement Speed. Difficult terrain, crawling, swimming, and climbing cost twice the normal movement distance unless an ability states otherwise. Standing from prone costs half the

character's Movement Speed. Diagonal movement is measured using ordinary distance. Movement Speed is not directly increased by ability score modifiers. Class abilities, mutations, equipment, and temporary effects may modify movement. Combat Philosophy Combat in 501 Rads is intended to be volatile, decisive, and dangerous. Even successful encounters may leave combatants injured or dead. Characters are expected to be hit relatively frequently, and victory should depend on preparation, positioning, equipment, teamwork, and the effective use of abilities rather than simply having a large pool of HP. As characters advance, their defenses and survivability improve considerably, but higher-level enemies become correspondingly more dangerous. Powerful enemies should threaten experienced characters through devastating attacks, unusual abilities, and tactical

advantages rather than relying exclusively on enormous HP pools. Actions, Class Resources, and Saving Throws Class Resource Generation Each class possesses a unique resource used to activate its special abilities: Heat (Gunslinger), Tolerance (Psycho), Access (Hacker), Malpractice (Medic), Authority (Soldier), or Faith (Prophet). These resources are earned through meaningful actions, successful checks, and class-specific accomplishments, as described in each class's rules. Resource farming is prohibited. Characters cannot repeatedly perform trivial, inconsequential, or substantially identical actions for the purpose of generating class resources. The Game Master determines whether an action meaningfully qualifies for a resource

award. Multiple resource awards may result from a single event when the qualifying accomplishments are distinct, such as landing a killing blow that awards resources for both hitting and defeating an enemy. Resources are awarded after the triggering action resolves. Characters cannot spend more resources than they currently possess, and cannot accumulate resources beyond their class's current maximum. Class resources reset to zero following a long rest. Class Ability Clarifications All classes share the same two initial class abilities, though under different names. Unlike all other class abilities, which require either a reactor or skill action point to use, these abilities cost no action points to use, and are used in conjunction with other events. For either of them, you may use them any time you

are prompted to roll a check. Stacking Resource Triggers A single action may generate class resources from multiple qualifying triggers. Each distinct trigger awards its full resource amount. For example, a Hacker who successfully bypasses an electronic security system using an Intelligence-based Hacking check earns: ●+1 Access for succeeding on an Intelligence check. ●+1 Access for successfully bypassing an electronic security system. ●Total: +2 Access. This applies to all classes. Resource generation remains subject to the character's maximum resource capacity and the existing prohibition against farming resources through trivial or repetitive actions. Class resources generated in excess of the maximum simply do nothing.

Action Economy During each combat turn, a character receives the following: Turn Component Quantity Purpose Action 1 Attack, perform a complex task, interact with the environment, or take another substantial action Movement 1 Move up to the character's Movement Speed Bonus Action 1 Perform a quick action, minor interaction, or maneuver permitted by the rules Skill Action 1 Activate a class ability, whether or not it consumes class resources

Reaction 1 per round Respond to an event using an ability or action that explicitly permits a reaction Characters may perform their available turn components in any order and may divide their movement before, between, or after other actions. Unused actions do not carry over into future turns. Skill Actions are reserved for activating class abilities. Activating an ability normally consumes one Skill Action, regardless of its resource cost. Passive class abilities function automatically and do not consume Skill Actions. Abilities with specified preparation times, such as surgery or lengthy technical procedures, still require that time to complete. Reactions occur in response to specific triggering events, including events outside the character's own turn. A character regains their Reaction at the beginning of their next turn. Class abilities explicitly described as

reactions consume a Reaction instead of a Skill Action, unless otherwise stated. Effect Stacking: Multiple instances of the same effect do not stack unless explicitly stated otherwise. Reapplying an effect refreshes its duration but does not increase its strength. Different effects may stack, even when they provide similar benefits, unless their descriptions specify otherwise. Saving Throws When an ability requires a target to resist its effects, the target makes a saving throw using the ability score specified by that effect. The difficulty of resisting a character's ability is determined by the character using it: Ability Save DC = 8 + Relevant Ability Modifier + Proficiency Bonus The relevant ability modifier is determined by the class ability being used. It is generally

one of the class's primary ability scores, but individual abilities may specify otherwise. The defending creature rolls: Saving Throw = d20 + Relevant Saving Throw Modifier A saving throw succeeds when its result equals or exceeds the Ability Save DC. On a failure, the creature suffers the effect described by the ability. Unless otherwise stated, a successful save prevents the effect entirely. Proficiency Bonus Proficiency represents a character's developing competence and contributes to the difficulty of resisting their class abilities. Character Level Proficiency Bonus 1–4 +2

5–8 +3 9–12 +4 The proficiency bonus also applies to other proficient checks, attacks, and saving throws as specified by the broader rules. Ability Ranges All distances in 501 Rads are measured in feet. Unless an ability specifies otherwise, a creature must be within the stated range when the ability is activated. An ability that requires sight cannot target a creature behind an opaque obstruction, even if the creature is within range. Abilities that specify touch require physical contact. Abilities affecting the user alone have a range of Self. Abilities without a stated range or target requirement are governed by

their individual descriptions. Initiative When combat begins, every participant rolls Initiative: Initiative = d20 + Dexterity Modifier Combat proceeds from highest Initiative to lowest. Ties are resolved by the higher Dexterity score. Remaining ties are resolved by the Game Master. Each participant takes one turn per round. Once every participant has taken a turn, a new round begins in the same Initiative order. A round represents approximately six seconds. Surprise: A creature unaware of an imminent attack is Surprised. A Surprised creature cannot take Actions, Bonus Actions, Skill Actions, or Movement during its first turn, and cannot take Reactions until that turn ends.

The Game Master determines surprise based on circumstances, potentially using Stealth and Perception checks. Cover Cover represents physical obstacles that interfere with attacks. ●Partial Cover: +2 AC and +2 to Dexterity saving throws against effects obstructed by the cover. ●Substantial Cover: +5 AC and +5 to Dexterity saving throws against effects obstructed by the cover. ●Total Cover: A creature cannot be directly targeted by attacks originating on the opposite side of the obstruction. Cover bonuses do not stack. A creature benefits from only the strongest applicable cover. Cover applies based on the direction of the attack or effect. A creature may have cover from one attacker but not another.

Area effects may bypass cover when their point of origin is on the same side as the protected creature. Particularly powerful weapons may destroy cover, as determined by the Game Master. Conditions Condition Mechanical effect Blinded Disadvantage on attacks; attacks against you have advantage Deafened Cannot hear; automatically fail checks requiring hearing Poisoned Disadvantage on attacks and ability checks Prone Melee attacks within 5 ft have advantage; attacks from farther away

have disadvantage; standing costs half movement Restrained Movement 0; attacks against you have advantage; your attacks and DEX saves have disadvantage Stunned Cannot take Actions, Bonus Actions, Skill Actions, Movement, or Reactions; attacks against you have advantage Incapacitated Cannot take Actions, Bonus Actions, Skill Actions, or Reactions, but may move unless another effect prevents it Frightened Disadvantage on attacks and checks while the source of fear is visible; cannot willingly move closer Burning Takes 1d6 fire damage at the beginning of each turn until extinguished

Irradiated Subject to a radioactive side effect as specified by the source Entities affected with burning can spend 1 action to extinguish flames. Environmental effects, like bodies of water, can end the condition early.
Classes

Gunslinger The gunslinger is the wild, gun toting cowboy of the American wasteland. Quick, both in body and wit, the gunslinger relies on distraction, positioning, and wild antics to survive in the wasteland. Gunslingers specialize in pistols and grenades, as well as in charm and smooth talking.

Gunslingers are all about hot streaks. They always seem to get lucky, and their luck tends to last. It is recommended that gunslingers focus stat points into Dex and Cha. Enemies who make saving throws as a result of the Gunslinger’s abilities make those saves against the Gunslinger’s dexterity. Primary Class Feature: Gunslingers gain access to “heat” points. Gunslingers can earn heat points towards their hot streak, and spend those points to use powerful abilities. Gunslingers earn a heat point for any of the following, though dungeon masters can award extra points at will: +1 For a successful Charisma check or save +1 For a successful Dexterity check or save +1 For landing a hit with a pistol weapon

+1 For landing a hit with a grenade (stacks) +2 For killing an opponent with a pistol or grenade As the character levels up, they increase their maximum heat, as well as unlock new abilities with that heat. Heat resets after a long rest. Level 1: Level 1 gunslingers gain access to the first two heat abilities, and at level 1 have a max heat of 3. Lucky strike; for -1 heat, the user can re-roll any check. They must take the new value. Stroke of Genius; for -3 heat, the user can roll 3 dice instead of one for any check, and select which dice they wish. (It's like double advantage!) In addition, gunslingers get +1 to checks and damage rolls done with pistols.

Level 2: At level 2, gunslingers unlock the following Fan the Hammer; For -2 heat points, the gunslinger can fire several times in short succession. The gunslinger's next attack with a pistol has its damage multiplied by 3, but the gunslinger must announce before that attack that this ability is being used. You can still miss! Level 3: Max heat increases from 3 to 5, and the gunslinger unlocks the ability to wield two pistols at once. Both pistols may attack within the same action Level 4: At level 4, the gunslinger unlocks the following: Distraction: for -2 heat, the gunslinger can choose any target that a teammate has already done damage to since the gunslingers previous turn. That teammate has “distracted” this opponent. For the remainder of this turn, any

checks made to harm the target have advantage, and attacks made with pistols are guaranteed to hit. The same target cannot be distracted more than once. Pickpocket: for -2 heat, when outside or inside combat, the gunslinger can pickpocket any target. If the target is known to have something on their person, the gunslinger can grab it. Otherwise, they can grab something random from the target. The target rolls a D20 to detect the intrusion, and only is aware if they roll a perfect 20. Level 5: at level 5, max heat increases to 7 Deadeye: for -5 heat, the gunslinger chooses any non-boss target. On the gunslinger's next turn, if both the gunslinger and the target are still alive, and the gunslinger has line of sight to the target, the gunslinger fires a deadly shot. It always kills the target. To activate deadeye, you cannot take any other action, nor can you

move. Being moved by any means interrupts the effect, and the heat is not refunded. Level 6: At level 6, the gunslinger unlocks the following Shrouded attack: if the gunslinger is not detected by enemies, they gain advantage on checks to harm them Fantastic Story: for -4 heat, the gunslinger can cobble together a nonsensical story. Despite how crazy it sounds, a portion of it is true. The part of it that is true is at the DM’s discretion, but the effect is always helpful to the gunslinger. Gunslingers can tell fantastic stories to distract, persuade, or intimidate their enemies. Level 7: at level 7, max heat increases to 9, and the amount of heat added doubles whenever heat would be added. (i.e. +2 for successful checks, etc)

No one walks away: for -7 heat, the gunslinger pulls an excellent stunt. For any number of targets that the gunslinger can see, the gunslinger fires twice at them. There is no limit to the number of targets. Level 8: at level 8, the following effects are added Master Gambler: gunslingers have advantage on any check that involves the gambling of money or property Old friend: for -5 heat, the gambler happens upon an old friend. The friend is helpful, knowledgeable, and useful. They always have some favor they owe the gunslinger. The gunslinger has friends everywhere. Level 9: At level 9, max heat becomes 11

Bending Bullets: The gunslinger can now hit targets in cover/they cannot see by accidentally ricocheting shots into them. Attempts to hit in this way incur a -3 to hit penalty. Wild Plan: For -8 heat, the gunslinger can devise a wild plan. They alone have final say on that plan. As long as the steps of that plan are followed by the gunslinger and their teammates, any skill checks which follow the steps of the plan or advance the plan in some way have advantage. Level 10: At level 10, the following abilities are gained Super Deadeye: for -11 heat, any target, including bosses, can be targeted. If a boss is targeted, the effect works the same as normal deadeye. If a non-boss target is chosen, the gunslinger does not have to wait a full turn, the target simply dies.

Level 11: At level 11, there is no longer a maximum heat value. Unbelievable luck: For -10 heat, any non-plot item happens to be nearby. It might not be easy to get, but it will be there. It's almost like you wished it into existence Level 12: At level 12, the amount of heat added triples whenever heat would be added. (i.e. +3 for successful checks, etc) Divine Intervention: for -15 heat the gunslinger can wish for just about anything and somehow it happens. The ultimate stroke of luck. Each time this ability is used, the probability that an unintended consequence occurs increases. Psycho The Psycho is the eternal drug overdose who feels no pain (because of the drugs). They

tactically mix drugs to become the ultimate utility, but usually that utility is violent and loud Psychos are about pushing their system to the limit, taking as many drugs as they can tolerate It is recommended that psychos focus stat points into Str and Cha. Enemies who make saving throws as a result of the Psycho’s abilities make those saves against the Psycho’s Strength. If a psycho refreshes an ability that would incur a negative side effect upon its termination, that negative side effect is delayed, and the duration of the negative side effect is unchanged. The same is true for the side effects of normal consumable drugs, an ability which is unique to the Psycho. Keep reupping those drugs!

Primary Class Feature: Psychos gain access to “tolerance” points. Psychos can earn tolerance points towards taking more powerful drugs, and spend those points to use powerful abilities. Psychos earn a tolerance point for any of the following, though dungeon masters can award extra points at will: +1 For a successful Charisma check or save +1 For a successful Strength check or save +1 For landing a hit with a melee weapon +1 For landing a hit with a chemical weapon(stacks) +2 For killing an opponent with a melee or chemical weapon As the character levels up, they increase their maximum tolerance, as well as unlock new abilities with that tolerance. Tolerance resets after a long rest.

Level 1: Level 1 psychos gain access to the first two tolerance abilities, and at level 1 have a max tolerance of 3. Ibuprofen; for -1 tolerance, the user can re-roll any check. They must take the new value. Cocaine; for -3 tolerance, the user can roll 3 dice instead of one for any check, and select which dice they wish. (It's like double advantage!) In addition, Psychos get +1 to checks and damage rolls done with melee weaponry. Level 2: At level 2, psychos unlock the following Heroin; For -2 tolerance points, the psycho reduces all incoming damage taken until their next turn by half. During this time, they have disadvantage on dexterity based checks.

Level 3: Max tolerance increases from 3 to 5, and the psycho unlocks the ability to wield furniture and other environmental objects as a melee weapon. Environmental weapons are up to DM discretion for power levels, but are usually surprisingly effective. Level 4: At level 4, the psycho unlocks the following: Meth: for -2 tolerance, the psycho can double his movement speed for three turns, as well as increase melee attack checks by +2. The user gets disadvantage on intelligence checks during the duration of the effect. Activating this ability while it is active extends the duration, but does not stack. IntelliBoostPro: for -2 tolerance, the psycho gains advantage on all intelligence checks for 5 minutes, but disadvantage on strength checks during the span. When the effect ends, the effect flips, and the psycho gains advantage on strength

checks and disadvantage on intelligence checks, also for 5 minutes. Level 5: at level 5, max tolerance increases to 7 Bromo-Dragonfly: for -5 tolerance, the psycho begins hallucinating. While hallucinating, the psycho can see the weak points of nearby people and objects, as well as the locations of nearby valuable items. While hallucinating, if the user takes any damage, their trip turns evil, and they must attack the nearest target every 15 seconds. The trip lasts 3 minutes. Level 6: At level 6, the psycho unlocks the following Incredible Intimidation: The mere presence of a psycho is unnerving. For each unspent tolerance point, the psycho gets +2 to intimidation checks.

DMT: for -4 tolerance, the psycho can see the emotions of everyone around them. They can tell a person is sad, angry, etc from far away with perfect accuracy, can detect lies, and can see particularly strong emotions through walls. Because of visual distortion, they have disadvantage on any check that relies on normal vision. This effect lasts 30 minutes. Level 7: at level 7, max tolerance increases to 9, and the amount of tolerance added doubles whenever tolerance would be added. (i.e. +2 for successful checks, etc) SuperSoldier: for -7 tolerance, the psycho flies into a combat rage. For the next 3 turns, they may take either an extra action or bonus action, move twice as fast, and have advantage on attack rolls. Once the 3 turns end, they pass out, and are unconscious for 2 turns. Level 8: at level 8, the following effects are added

Chemical Immunity: the psycho becomes immune to inhaled or ingested poisons or chemicals, and can identify chemicals by tasting them. OmegaMax: for -5 tolerance, the psycho becomes able to camouflage. It only works effectively when staying still, but is very effective when conditions are met. It lasts 20 mins, and at the end, the psycho glows bright green for 2 mins. Level 9: At level 9, max tolerance becomes 11 Rage: Not being on drugs makes you really angry. You get +2 to strength checks per unspent tolerance, but -1 to intelligence, wisdom, and dexterity checks per unspent tolerance. Jericho: For -8 tolerance, the psycho becomes obsessed with a target. While the effect is active, all checks made to harm the target are made with advantage, the psycho knows the precise location of the target, and deals double

damage to the target. While the effect is active, the psycho may not do any actions that don't result in harm to the target. The effect lasts 3 minutes or until the target is dead. Level 10: At level 10, the following abilities are gained UltraSoldier: for -11 tolerance, the psycho flies into an ultra combat rage. For the next 3 turns, they may take a sum of two additional actions or bonus actions, move three times as fast, and have advantage on attack rolls, and +4 on damage rolls. Once the 3 turns end, they pass out, and are unconscious for 3 turns. Level 11: At level 11, there is no longer a maximum tolerance value. Wrecking Ball: For -10 tolerance, the psycho gains the ability to run through solid objects as long as they are reasonably thin. This includes enemies, which they can run into to

deal damage and push away. This effect lasts 3 minutes. Level 12: At level 12, the amount of tolerance added triples whenever tolerance would be added. (i.e. +3 for successful checks, etc) UltraCocaMethMorphine: for -15 tolerance the psycho becomes invincible and immortal for 3 minutes. Hacker The Hacker is the technologically gifted menace of the American wasteland. While most wastelanders consider a functioning toaster to be a technological marvel, the Hacker is busy breaking into military computers, hijacking security robots, and figuring out how to make that toaster launch nuclear missiles. Hackers specialize in computers, electronics, mechanical devices, and the delicate art of making

expensive things do things they were never intended to do. Hackers are all about access. Every successful intrusion, clever modification, or technological breakthrough gives them another foothold in the systems around them. The more access they gain, the more spectacular their exploits become. It is recommended that Hackers focus stat points into Int and Dex. Enemies who make saving throws as a result of the Hackers abilities make those saves against the Hacker’s intelligence Primary Class Feature: Hackers gain access to "Access" points. Hackers can earn Access points through successful technical actions and spend those points to use powerful abilities. Hackers earn an Access point for any of the following, though dungeon masters can award extra points at will: +1 For a successful Intelligence check or save

+1 For a successful Dexterity check or save +1 For successfully hacking or bypassing an electronic security system +1 For successfully disabling, repairing, or modifying a technological device +1 For landing a hit with an electronic or energy weapon +2 For successfully taking control of a hostile electronic system or robotic enemy As the character levels up, they increase their maximum Access, as well as unlock new abilities with that Access. Access resets after a long rest. Level 1: Level 1 Hackers gain access to the first two Access abilities, and at level 1 have a max Access of 3. Have You Tried Turning It Off and On Again? For -1 Access, the Hacker can reroll any check. They must take the new value.

Administrator Privileges: For -3 Access, the Hacker can roll 3 dice instead of one for any check, and select which die they wish. In addition, Hackers get +1 to checks involving hacking, repairing, or modifying electronic devices. Level 2: At level 2, Hackers unlock the following: Remote Access: For -2 Access, the Hacker can remotely interact with any electronic device they can see within 100 feet, as though they were physically connected to it. This includes computers, electronic locks, cameras, terminals, and similar devices. The Hacker must still make any checks ordinarily required to manipulate the device, and cannot access systems that have no electronic interface. Level 3: Max Access increases from 3 to 5, and the Hacker unlocks the ability to construct improvised electronic devices from scavenged components. These devices can perform simple

functions such as recording audio, transmitting signals, detecting movement, or activating mechanical switches. The GM determines what components are required, but Hackers are exceptionally good at finding substitutes. Level 4: At level 4, the Hacker unlocks the following: Backdoor: For -2 Access, the Hacker can establish a hidden connection to an electronic system they have successfully accessed. For the next 24 hours, they can reconnect to that system without repeating the original security checks, provided the system remains operational and within communication range. Only one Backdoor may be maintained at a time. Deepfake: For -2 Access, the Hacker can manipulate an electronic recording, image, or transmission to convincingly imitate another person, fabricate an event, or conceal information. The resulting forgery is convincing to ordinary observers, although sophisticated forensic examination may reveal inconsistencies.

Level 5: At level 5, max Access increases to 7. Ghost in the Machine: For -5 Access, the Hacker can temporarily seize control of a nearby robotic device, automated turret, security drone, or similar machine for 5 minutes. The target must be electronically accessible and cannot be substantially more sophisticated than the Hacker's available equipment. While controlled, the machine obeys the Hacker's commands, although intelligent machines may attempt to resist or regain control at the GM's discretion. Level 6: At level 6, the Hacker unlocks the following: Technological Intuition: The Hacker can determine the general purpose, operational condition, and likely weaknesses of any technological device after examining it for one minute. They can also identify whether a device has been tampered with, sabotaged, or modified.

Digital Archaeology: For -4 Access, the Hacker can recover information from a damaged, corrupted, or partially destroyed electronic storage device. The recovered information may be incomplete, but always includes something useful if the device originally contained relevant data. The GM determines exactly what survives. Level 7: At level 7, max Access increases to 9, and the amount of Access added doubles whenever Access would be added. System Override: For -7 Access, the Hacker can seize control of all electronically controlled devices connected to a single local network for 3 minutes. This may include doors, cameras, alarms, lighting, automated defenses, and industrial equipment. Devices physically disconnected from the network are unaffected. Highly sophisticated security systems may resist particularly dangerous commands. Level 8: At level 8, the following effects are added:

Walking Encyclopedia: Hackers have advantage on Intelligence checks involving pre-war technology, computer systems, robotics, and electronic infrastructure. They can also recognize the manufacturer and likely purpose of most surviving technological equipment. Identity Theft: For -5 Access, the Hacker can fabricate a convincing electronic identity within a system they have accessed. For the next 24 hours, automated systems treat the Hacker as an authorized user with a plausible clearance level. Human observers may still become suspicious if the Hacker behaves inconsistently with their supposed identity. Level 9: At level 9, max Access becomes 11. Wireless Menace: The Hacker can now remotely access electronic systems within 350 feet, even without direct line of sight, provided they can detect or identify the target's electronic signal. Remote Access no longer requires visual contact.

Skeleton Key: For -8 Access, the Hacker can bypass almost any electronic security system they can access, including sophisticated military locks, encrypted databases, and corporate authentication systems. The bypass succeeds automatically unless the system is protected by an extraordinary or plot-critical security measure. The Hacker does not necessarily gain control of everything behind the security system. Level 10: At level 10, the following abilities are gained: Total System Failure: For -11 Access, the Hacker can cause a catastrophic malfunction in a technological system they can access. A power grid might collapse, an automated factory might destroy itself, or a military installation's defenses might turn against their operators. The GM determines the exact consequences based on the system's capabilities. The effect cannot create functions the system was never capable of performing.

Level 11: At level 11, there is no longer a maximum Access value. I Know a Guy Who Knows a Guy: For -10 Access, the Hacker discovers a useful connection within an existing technological or communications network. This might be a forgotten administrative account, an abandoned maintenance terminal, a dormant satellite connection, or an overlooked communications relay. The connection always provides a meaningful advantage, although accessing it may require additional work. Level 12: At level 12, the amount of Access added triples whenever Access would be added. Root Access: For -15 Access, the Hacker gains near-absolute control over a single technological system they can access for 10 minutes. During this time, the Hacker can issue commands that bypass ordinary software restrictions, override security protocols, and exploit capabilities that even the system's designers may not have anticipated. The system must remain physically capable of performing the

requested actions, and the GM determines the consequences of particularly extraordinary commands. This can include vehicles, robots, factories, all sorts of things. Medic The Medic is the wasteland's foremost expert on the human body, or at least the foremost expert willing to operate without a license. A brilliant surgeon, deranged biologist, and walking violation of medical ethics, the Medic views the human body as an extraordinarily complicated machine that could probably be improved with enough scalpels, chemicals, and screaming. Medics specialize in healing, biological experimentation, surgery, poisons, and the manipulation of living organisms. They can transform their allies into medical miracles and their enemies into cautionary tales.

Medics are all about malpractice. Every successful procedure, questionable experiment, and spectacular violation of the Hippocratic Oath brings them closer to their next breakthrough. Their methods may be horrifying, but their results are difficult to argue with. It is recommended that Medics focus stat points into Con and Int. Enemies who make saving throws as a result of the Medics abilities make those saves against the Medic’s intelligence. Primary Class Feature: Medics gain access to "Malpractice" points. Medics can earn Malpractice through successful medical actions and spend those points to perform powerful biological procedures. Medics earn a Malpractice point for any of the following, though dungeon masters can award extra points at will: +1 For a successful Intelligence check or save +1 For a successful Constitution check or save

+1 For successfully diagnosing or treating an injury, illness, or biological condition +1 For successfully administering a drug, poison, or biological treatment to another creature +1 For successfully extracting useful biological information or material from a living organism +2 For successfully saving a creature at less than 10% their base hp by raising their hp above 50% or incapacitating an enemy through a biological effect As the character levels up, they increase their maximum Malpractice, as well as unlock new abilities with that Malpractice. Malpractice resets after a long rest. Level 1: Level 1 Medics gain access to the first two Malpractice abilities, and at level 1 have a max Malpractice of 3. Second Opinion: For -1 Malpractice, the Medic can reroll any check. They must take the new value.

Clinical Trial: For -3 Malpractice, the Medic can roll 3 dice instead of one for any check, and select which die they wish. In addition, Medics get +1 to checks involving medicine, surgery, diagnosis, and the administration of biological treatments. Level 2: At level 2, Medics unlock the following: Questionable Prescription: For -2 Malpractice, the Medic administers a custom pharmaceutical cocktail to themselves or a willing creature they can touch. For the next 10 minutes, the recipient gains advantage on checks using one ability score of the Medic's choice. During this time, they have disadvantage on checks using another ability score, also chosen by the Medic. The recipient must be informed of neither choice. Level 3: Max Malpractice increases from 3 to 5, and the Medic unlocks the ability to perform surgery under almost any circumstances. The

Medic can use improvised tools, perform procedures without a sterile environment, and stabilize critically injured patients using materials ordinarily considered unsuitable for medical purposes. The GM determines the difficulty of particularly extraordinary procedures. Level 4: At level 4, the Medic unlocks the following: Performance Enhancing Drugs: For -2 Malpractice, the Medic can inject themselves or a willing creature with an experimental stimulant. For the next 3 turns, the recipient gains +2 to attack checks and doubles their movement speed. When the effect ends, the recipient suffers disadvantage on Dexterity and Strength checks for 3 turns. Repeated applications extend the duration but do not stack. Medical Examination: For -2 Malpractice, the Medic can determine the physical condition of any living creature they can examine for at least 30 seconds. The Medic learns about

injuries, diseases, poisons, mutations, biological weaknesses, and unusual physiological characteristics. They can also determine whether the creature has recently been exposed to radiation, drugs, or other biological contaminants. Particularly unusual conditions may require further investigation. Level 5: At level 5, max Malpractice increases to 7. Organ Donation: For -5 Malpractice, the Medic can temporarily transfer a biological characteristic from one willing creature to another. The Medic may transfer a sense, a natural physical adaptation, or a minor beneficial mutation. The donor loses access to the transferred characteristic for the duration, while the recipient gains it. The effect lasts 10 minutes, after which both creatures return to normal. The procedure cannot transfer major organs necessary for survival or extraordinary mutations at the GM's discretion. The procedure cannot ever transfer any effect or ability that

the target already has. If it does, there is no stacking, and the ability is effectively ignored. For example, giving someone an extra nose doesn’t make them smell twice as well. Level 6: At level 6, the Medic unlocks the following: Anatomical Expertise: The Medic has advantage on checks involving identifying biological weaknesses, treating injuries, understanding unfamiliar organisms, and determining causes of death. Additionally, the Medic can identify the approximate age, health, and biological condition of a creature through careful observation. Unlicensed Experimentation: For -4 Malpractice, the Medic can temporarily alter the physiology of a willing creature for 30 minutes. The Medic may give the recipient one of the following adaptations: the ability to breathe underwater, immunity to ordinary environmental temperatures, enhanced night vision, or the ability to survive without breathing. When the effect ends, the

recipient suffers a harmless but conspicuous biological side effect determined by the GM. Level 7: At level 7, max Malpractice increases to 9, and the amount of Malpractice added doubles whenever Malpractice would be added. Hippocratic Suggestion: For -7 Malpractice, the Medic can administer a powerful neurochemical treatment to a living creature they can touch. For the next 5 minutes, the target becomes extremely susceptible to suggestion and treats the Medic as a trusted medical authority. The Medic may issue reasonable instructions that the target will attempt to follow. Instructions that directly threaten the target's life or fundamentally contradict its strongest convictions may be resisted through a Wisdom save. Level 8: At level 8, the following effects are added: Doctor's Orders: The Medic has advantage on Charisma checks when presenting themselves as a

medical professional, explaining medical procedures, or convincing others that a situation constitutes a medical emergency. This applies even when the Medic's qualifications are completely fabricated. Biological Sabotage: For -5 Malpractice, the Medic can administer a specialized biological agent to a living target they can touch or successfully inject. The target suffers one effect chosen by the Medic for 5 minutes: temporary blindness, loss of speech, severely reduced movement speed, or uncontrollable muscle spasms. The target may attempt a Constitution save to resist the effect. The procedure causes no permanent injury unless the GM determines otherwise. Level 9: At level 9, max Malpractice becomes 11. Mutational Medicine: The Medic gains the ability to temporarily suppress one negative mutation affecting a willing creature for 30 minutes. This requires one minute of examination and treatment. The mutation returns when the effect

ends. A creature can only benefit from one such suppression at a time. Experimental Evolution: For -8 Malpractice, the Medic can temporarily amplify one positive mutation possessed by a willing creature for 10 minutes. The GM determines how the mutation improves, but the enhancement should be substantial and appropriate to the original effect. When the treatment ends, the mutation becomes inactive for 10 minutes as the recipient's body recovers. Level 10: At level 10, the following abilities are gained: Catastrophic Diagnosis: For -11 Malpractice, the Medic can identify and exploit a devastating biological vulnerability in a living creature they can observe. The Medic selects one target and announces a diagnosis. For the next 3 turns, the target suffers disadvantage on all physical checks and saves, takes double damage from attacks, and cannot regain HP through ordinary healing. The target may attempt a Constitution

save at the beginning of each turn to end the effect. The Medic must be able to see the target when activating this ability. Level 11: At level 11, there is no longer a maximum Malpractice value. Medical Miracle: For -10 Malpractice, the Medic can perform an extraordinary biological procedure that would ordinarily be considered impossible. Examples include restoring a lost limb, curing an otherwise incurable disease, reversing severe biological damage, or reconstructing a critically damaged organ. The procedure requires appropriate materials and at least 10 minutes of uninterrupted work. It cannot reverse death or permanently remove the radiation infection central to the campaign. Level 12: At level 12, the amount of Malpractice added triples whenever Malpractice would be added. God Complex: For -15 Malpractice, the Medic can completely rewrite the biological condition of a

single living creature they can touch. For the next 10 minutes, the Medic may impose extraordinary biological changes, including granting temporary physical adaptations, disabling major bodily functions, radically altering the creature's appearance, or transforming its physiology in ways that defy conventional medicine. The changes must be biological in nature, and the GM determines the limits of particularly extreme transformations. Unwilling targets may attempt a Constitution save to resist the procedure. When the effect ends, the target returns to its original biological state, although the experience may leave lasting psychological consequences. Soldier The Soldier is a highly trained instrument of war, or at least someone who has spent enough

time around military equipment to convincingly impersonate one. A master of battlefield tactics, leadership, and organized violence, the Soldier understands that victory is rarely achieved through individual heroics. It is achieved through discipline, preparation, and convincing everyone else to do exactly what they're told. Soldiers specialize in rifles, heavy weapons, defensive positions, leadership, and the coordination of their allies. They are equally comfortable organizing an assault on a fortified compound, training a group of terrified civilians, or explaining to an enemy why surrendering immediately would be in everyone's best interest. Soldiers are all about authority. Every successful maneuver, decisive order, and demonstration of tactical competence strengthens their command over the battlefield. The more Authority they accumulate, the more extraordinary their leadership becomes.

It is recommended that Soldiers focus stat points into Str and Wis. Enemies who make saving throws as a result of the Soldiers abilities make those saves against the soldier’s wisdom Primary Class Feature: Soldiers gain access to "Authority" points. Soldiers earn Authority through successful physical actions, tactical decisions, and leadership, and spend those points to use powerful abilities. Soldiers earn an Authority point for any of the following, though dungeon masters can award extra points at will: +1 For a successful Strength check or save +1 For a successful Wisdom check or save +1 For successfully assisting an ally with a check +1 For landing a hit with a rifle or heavy weapon

+1 For successfully identifying or exploiting a tactical advantage +2 For defeating an enemy through a coordinated attack involving at least one ally As the character levels up, they increase their maximum Authority, as well as unlock new abilities with that Authority. Authority resets after a long rest. Level 1: Level 1 Soldiers gain access to the first two Authority abilities, and at level 1 have a max Authority of 3. Second Attempt, Soldier! For -1 Authority, the Soldier can reroll any check. They must take the new value. Military Precision: For -3 Authority, the Soldier can roll 3 dice instead of one for any check, and select which die they wish. In addition, Soldiers get +1 to checks and damage rolls made with rifles and heavy weapons.

Level 2: At level 2, Soldiers unlock the following: Follow My Lead: For -2 Authority, the Soldier can designate one willing ally they can communicate with. For the next 3 turns, whenever the Soldier successfully makes a check using Strength or Wisdom, that ally gains advantage on their next check involving a similar task. Outside combat, this ability lasts 5 minutes. Level 3: Max Authority increases from 3 to 5, and the Soldier unlocks the ability to use heavy weapons without suffering ordinary handling penalties. Additionally, the Soldier can organize improvised defensive positions using nearby terrain and materials. Given 10 minutes of preparation, the Soldier can create a defensible position that grants cover to nearby allies, subject to the environment and available resources. Level 4: At level 4, the Soldier unlocks the following:

Suppressing Fire: For -2 Authority, the Soldier can designate an area they can see and fire a sustained burst of weapon fire into it. Until the beginning of their next turn, enemies attempting to move through the designated area must succeed on a Wisdom save or abandon their movement. Enemies that remain in cover are unaffected. Command Presence: For -2 Authority, the Soldier can issue an authoritative command to a group of creatures who can hear and understand them. For the next 5 minutes, the Soldier gains advantage on Charisma checks involving organizing, directing, or negotiating with that group. Creatures who are actively hostile may resist the effect through a Wisdom save. Level 5: At level 5, max Authority increases to 7. Coordinated Assault: For -5 Authority, the Soldier can organize a coordinated attack involving themselves and up to three willing allies. Each participant may immediately make one attack against a target of their choice,

provided they are capable of attacking and can receive the Soldier's orders. These attacks have advantage. Each participant may only benefit from this ability once per round. Level 6: At level 6, the Soldier unlocks the following: Veteran's Instinct: The Soldier has advantage on Wisdom checks involving detecting ambushes, identifying military equipment, recognizing tactical formations, or evaluating the defensibility of a location. Additionally, the Soldier can determine whether an armed group appears professionally trained after observing them briefly. Emergency Requisition: For -4 Authority, the Soldier can locate a useful piece of military equipment among nearby supplies, abandoned structures, or accessible storage. The item must plausibly exist in the area and cannot be exceptionally rare or plot-critical. The GM determines exactly where it is found, but the Soldier always knows where to look.

Level 7: At level 7, max Authority increases to 9, and the amount of Authority added doubles whenever Authority would be added. Hold the Line: For -7 Authority, the Soldier can establish an extraordinarily effective defensive position. For the next 3 turns, the Soldier and up to five willing allies within 45 feet gain advantage on defensive saves and take half damage from ranged attacks while remaining in their designated positions. The effect ends for any participant who abandons their position. Level 8: At level 8, the following effects are added: Drill Sergeant: The Soldier can train willing creatures in basic combat skills, weapon handling, and battlefield discipline. After one hour of instruction, up to ten creatures gain +2 to their next three attack checks or relevant physical checks. The benefit expires after 24 hours.

Chain of Command: For -5 Authority, the Soldier can temporarily convince a group of non-hostile armed personnel that they possess legitimate military authority. For the next 10 minutes, the group treats the Soldier as a superior officer unless presented with convincing evidence otherwise. The effect works best on organized military or paramilitary groups and may fail against individuals who personally know the actual chain of command. Level 9: At level 9, max Authority becomes 11. Perfect Formation: The Soldier and willing allies within 30 feet of them can move through crowded or dangerous environments without interfering with one another. Allies do not obstruct each other's movement or lines of fire, and the group gains advantage on checks involving coordinated movement, tactical positioning, or organized retreats. Tactical Genius: For -8 Authority, the Soldier can devise a comprehensive plan for a specific objective. The Soldier identifies up to five steps

required to accomplish that objective. For the next hour, all willing participants gain advantage on checks directly related to carrying out those steps, provided the plan remains reasonably applicable to the situation. Unexpected complications do not automatically invalidate the plan. Level 10: At level 10, the following abilities are gained: Total Mobilization: For -11 Authority, the Soldier grants each member of their party an extra turn, and the turns can be sequenced according to the soldier. Level 11: At level 11, there is no longer a maximum Authority value. Military Intelligence: For -10 Authority, the Soldier can deduce a significant weakness in an enemy organization, fortified location, or planned operation after studying available information for at least one minute. The GM reveals a meaningful vulnerability, overlooked

route, logistical problem, or tactical opportunity that the Soldier can exploit. The information must be accurate, although acting upon it may still be dangerous. Level 12: At level 12, the amount of Authority added triples whenever Authority would be added. Supreme Commander: For -15 Authority, the Soldier can issue a single extraordinary order to any number of willing creatures who can receive it. For the next 10 minutes, those creatures perform the ordered objective with nearly supernatural discipline and coordination. Participants gain advantage on all checks directly related to the objective, ignore ordinary fear and intimidation, and may act in coordinated sequences that would otherwise be impossible. The GM determines the limits of particularly extraordinary orders, but the ability cannot force unwilling creatures to obey or make physically impossible actions possible.

Prophet The Prophet is a wandering sharpshooter of the nuclear wasteland, a holy warrior whose sacred scriptures are written in gunpowder and whose sermons are delivered at several thousand feet per second. Whether their faith comes from a surviving prewar religion, an apocalyptic cult, or a revelation received after drinking radioactive groundwater, the Prophet is absolutely convinced that a higher power guides their hand. Prophets specialize in precision weapons, observation, religious influence, patience, and the elimination of enemies from extraordinary distances. They are equally comfortable delivering an impassioned sermon, identifying a sinner in a crowded settlement, or spending fourteen hours motionless on a rooftop waiting for divine permission to pull the trigger. Prophets are all about Faith. Every fulfilled prophecy, successful shot, and demonstration of

religious conviction strengthens their certainty that the universe is on their side. The more Faith they accumulate, the more difficult it becomes to distinguish their marksmanship from genuine divine intervention. It is recommended that Prophets focus stat points into Dex and Wis. Enemies who make saving throws as a result of the Prophets abilities make those saves against the Prophet’s wisdom Primary Class Feature: Prophets gain access to "Faith" points. Prophets earn Faith through successful acts of perception, precision, and religious devotion, and spend those points to perform extraordinary feats. Prophets earn a Faith point for any of the following, though dungeon masters can award extra points at will: +1 For a successful Dexterity check or save +1 For a successful Wisdom check or save

+1 For successfully identifying a hidden enemy, trap, or important detail through observation +1 For landing an attack with a precision or scoped weapon +1 For successfully persuading, inspiring, or intimidating another creature through religious conviction +2 For eliminating a dangerous enemy with a single carefully aimed shot As the character levels up, they increase their maximum Faith, as well as unlock new abilities with that Faith. Faith resets after a long rest. Level 1: Level 1 Prophets gain access to the first two Faith abilities, and at level 1 have a max Faith of 3. Divine Guidance: For -1 Faith, the Prophet can reroll any check. They must take the new value. The Lord Provides: For -3 Faith, the Prophet can roll 3 dice instead of one for any check, and select which die they wish.

In addition, Prophets gain +1 to attack checks made with precision rifles and +1 to Wisdom checks involving observation or religious knowledge. Level 2: At level 2, Prophets unlock the following: Mark of the Heretic: For -2 Faith, the Prophet can declare a creature they can see to be a heretic. For the next 10 minutes, the Prophet always knows the target's approximate direction while it remains within 300 Feet, and gains advantage on their first attack against that target. Only one creature can be marked at a time. Level 3: Max Faith increases from 3 to 5, and the Prophet gains the ability to interpret omens in ordinary events. After spending one minute examining an environment, the Prophet may ask the GM whether a particular course of action appears favorable, unfavorable, or uncertain. The GM must answer truthfully based on the information available, though the interpretation

may be cryptic. This ability may be used once per long rest without spending Faith. Level 4: At level 4, the Prophet unlocks the following: Blessed Ammunition: For -2 Faith, the Prophet can bless up to three rounds of ammunition. For the next hour, attacks made with those rounds ignore ordinary cover penalties and count as extraordinary or sanctified attacks against creatures resistant to conventional weaponry. Unused blessed ammunition loses its blessing after one hour. Street Preacher: For -2 Faith, the Prophet can deliver an impassioned sermon to creatures capable of understanding them. After one minute of preaching, the Prophet gains advantage on Charisma checks involving persuasion, intimidation, or inspiring the audience for the next 10 minutes. Hostile audiences may resist through a Wisdom save. Level 5: At level 5, max Faith increases to 7.

The Lord Works in Mysterious Ways: For -5 Faith, the Prophet can declare that an unlikely event is a sign of divine intervention. The GM introduces a plausible but highly fortunate coincidence that advances the Prophet's immediate objective. Examples include a guard abandoning their post, a locked door being left open, or an enemy's weapon unexpectedly malfunctioning. The coincidence cannot directly kill a creature or resolve a major plot objective by itself. Level 6: At level 6, the Prophet unlocks the following: Eye of Providence: The Prophet has advantage on Wisdom checks involving detecting concealed creatures, spotting distant details, recognizing deception, and identifying suspicious behavior. Additionally, the Prophet can accurately estimate distances to visible targets without special equipment. Confession: For -4 Faith, the Prophet can confront a creature they can communicate with

and demand that it confess its sins. The target must make a Wisdom save. On a failure, it feels an overwhelming compulsion to truthfully reveal one significant wrongdoing, secret, or source of guilt. The target chooses which truth to reveal, and the Prophet cannot specify the information disclosed. A successful save makes the creature immune to this ability for 24 hours. Level 7: At level 7, max Faith increases to 9, and the amount of Faith added doubles whenever Faith would be added. Judgment Day: For -7 Faith, the Prophet may designate a creature they can see as the subject of divine judgment. For the next 3 turns, the Prophet's ranged attacks against that creature ignore ordinary cover penalties, have advantage, and deal double damage. The effect ends if the target dies or the duration expires. Level 8: At level 8, the following effects are added:

Unshakable Conviction: The Prophet has advantage on saves against fear, intimidation, and attempts to undermine their beliefs. Additionally, the Prophet can remain perfectly still and alert for extraordinarily long periods without suffering ordinary discomfort or loss of concentration. Pilgrimage: For -5 Faith, the Prophet may pray for guidance toward a specific person, object, or location that they have sufficient reason to believe exists. The GM provides a meaningful clue about where or how it might be found. This may take the form of a vision, an overheard conversation, an unexpected discovery, or an apparent coincidence. The ability does not guarantee that the destination is safe or accessible. Level 9: At level 9, max Faith becomes 11. The Gospel According to Ballistics: The Prophet no longer suffers ordinary penalties for attacking targets at extreme range, provided they can clearly see the target and their weapon

is physically capable of reaching it. Additionally, the Prophet may use reflective surfaces, shadows, and environmental clues to identify targets who are not directly visible. Divine Retribution: For -8 Faith, when a creature the Prophet can see harms one of their allies, the Prophet may immediately make one ranged attack against that creature, even outside their normal turn. If the attack hits, it deals double damage. This ability cannot be used more than once per round. Level 10: At level 10, the following ability is gained: Thou Shalt Not Miss: For -11 Faith, the Prophet may declare a single ranged attack to be divinely ordained. If the target is within the physical range of the weapon and the Prophet has a plausible means of identifying its location, the attack automatically hits, regardless of ordinary cover, visibility, or accuracy penalties. The attack deals triple normal damage. Extraordinary defenses or major plot

protections may still apply at the GM's discretion. Level 11: At level 11, there is no longer a maximum Faith value. Prophet of the Wasteland: For -10 Faith, the Prophet can deliver a prophecy concerning a specific future event. The GM determines a plausible way in which the prophecy could become true and provides the Prophet with a cryptic revelation about the circumstances. For the next 24 hours, the Prophet and their allies gain advantage on checks directly related to bringing about or preventing that event. The prophecy cannot guarantee an impossible outcome. Level 12: At level 12, the amount of Faith added triples whenever Faith would be added. And God Said, Let There Be Lead: For -15 Faith, the Prophet may invoke divine judgment upon up to six creatures they can identify within the effective range of their weapon. The Prophet makes one ranged attack against each designated

creature, regardless of the weapon's normal firing rate or ammunition capacity. These attacks automatically hit and deal triple normal damage. During the attack, the Prophet may describe an extraordinary religious manifestation: a blinding halo, a chorus of distant angels, a thunderous voice from the heavens, or some other unmistakable sign of divine wrath. Whether this manifestation is genuinely supernatural, an extraordinary coincidence, or a shared hallucination is left to the GM. After the attack, the Prophet must spend their next turn reloading, praying, or otherwise recovering from the experience.

Ammunition and Reloading Ordinary ammunition is not tracked in 501 Rads. Characters are assumed to carry sufficient ammunition for their conventional weapons, and reloading occurs automatically as part of normal weapon use. Reloading does not consume an Action, Bonus Action, Skill Action, or Movement. This rule applies to ordinary ballistic ammunition, energy cells, chemical cartridges, and other standard weapon consumables. Heavy Explosive Ammunition: Particularly destructive weapons, including rocket launchers, missile launchers, and other heavy explosive

systems, require individually tracked ammunition. The Game Master determines which weapons fall into this category. Unusual weapons may have additional ammunition requirements when explicitly stated in their descriptions. Weapon Proficiencies Weapons are divided into four proficiency categories: Category Included Weapons Sidearms Pistols, revolvers, compact energy weapons, and similar one-handed firearms Long Guns Rifles, shotguns, sniper rifles, SMGs, and similar firearms Heavy Weapons Machine guns, rocket launchers, heavy energy weapons, and other cumbersome armaments Melee Weapons Knives, clubs, swords, improvised melee weapons, and unarmed combat

Characters add their Proficiency Bonus to attack rolls made with weapons belonging to categories in which they are proficient. Characters may use weapons outside their proficiencies, but do not add their Proficiency Bonus to those attacks. Additional weapon proficiencies may be acquired through feats or class abilities. Currency

There are three currencies recognized in the wasteland; Dollar ($) Chip (¢) Fusion Cell (FC) While vendors accept all three, the most common and de facto currency of the wasteland is Chips. Chips are small pieces of burnt out pre-war circuitry. Because the factories that produce them have been destroyed, no one can forge new ones, so people know chips are legit. Some people still use the pre-war dollar, but there are so many in circulation, they are very invaluable. 100 pre-war dollars is equivalent to one chip. The fusion cell is the highest tier of currency. Unlike the other two, fusion cells can be used

to power generators and vehicles, making them sought after as more than just a currency. Generally, fusion cells are worth 100 chips, and for large transactions are used as a bulk currency.
